processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Melted in a high-frequency vacuum induction furnace with a 50 kg capacity.
Cast into an ingot with a diameter of 150 mm.
Ingots were homogenized at 1200 °C for 5 h prior to hot rolling.
Hot rolled into rods with a diameter of 16 mm, then air-cooled to room temperature. This is the parent process (proc_hot-rolled).

The hot-rolled rods were additionally solution treated at 1100 °C for 2 h followed by water quenching (state 1100 °C–2 h–WQ). Applied to the Al-series to compare the effect of solution temperature (Fig. 2d, Fig. 8d).

structures.overall_structure: Fe30Mn6Al1C low-density steel after 1100 °C/2 h solution treatment + water quenching; the higher solution temperature coarsens the grains relative to the 1050 °C condition.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: round tensile specimen, gauge length 25 mm, diameter 5 mm (tensile axis parallel to rod axis); Charpy V-notch specimen 55 mm long, 10 × 10 mm cross-section, 2 mm deep V-notch
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile stress-strain responses and work-hardening rates obtained on solution-treated specimens; data are the average of two specimens; Charpy impact energy measured at -40 °C.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fig. 2(d): engineering stress-strain curves of Al-alloyed low-density steels (including Fe30Mn6Al1C) after solution treatment at 1100 °C for 2 h.

characterization_methods.technique: uniaxial tensile testing (engineering and true stress-strain curves with work-hardening-rate analysis)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: initial strain rate 1.1 × 10^-3 s^-1 at ambient temperature; round specimens with gauge length 25 mm and diameter 5 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: measure yield strength, tensile strength, elongation and work-hardening behaviour of the 1100 °C/2 h solution-treated Al-6 (Fe30Mn6Al1C) steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: Yield strength slightly lower than after the 1050 °C solution treatment (attributed to grain coarsening); the work-hardening-rate ordering with Al content is retained (6Al highest, 12Al lowest) and the true stress-strain curves extend to noticeably larger true strain than after 1050 °C (Fig. 2d, Fig. 8d).

unmapped_findings: No numeric mechanical property values are reported specifically for Fe30Mn6Al1C (Al-6) after the 1100 °C/2 h solution treatment; only the qualitative engineering stress-strain (Fig. 2d) and work-hardening-rate (Fig. 8d) curves are available for this condition.

The tabulated tensile/impact properties (Table 2) and microstructural parameters (Table 3, e.g. Al-6: D_FCC-G/T = 34.2 ± 1.1 μm, f_Tw = 45.3%, no ferrite, κ-carbide size 0 nm, impact toughness 354 ± 16 J) are reported for the 1050 °C/2 h solution-treated condition, NOT for this 1100 °C/2 h sample, and are therefore not assigned to this sample.

After 1100 °C/2 h solution treatment the yield strength of the Al-containing steels shows a slight decrease relative to the 1050 °C/2 h condition, which is attributed to an increase in grain size with increasing solution-treatment temperature (b0027).

For the Al-series at 1100 °C the work-hardening-rate ordering is retained (6% Al highest, 12% Al lowest) and the true stress-strain curves extend to noticeably larger true strain (some beyond 0.5) than after 1050 °C (Fig. 8d).
The ultimate true stress (σ_TS ≈ 1350 MPa) and fracture strength (σ_FS ≈ 2150 MPa) remain nearly unchanged for the 1100 °C solution-treated samples as well (b0075).

Consistent with Fig. 5, no κ-carbides were observed in the Fe30Mn(x)Al1C low-density steel at low Al content (8% Al shown as representative); Al-6 (6% Al) is the lowest-Al member with the highest reported impact toughness in the alloy series.
